questions.q: The image of the point with position vector $i+3 \mathbf{k}$ in the plane $r \cdot(i+j+k)=1$ is
questions.solution:
Let $Q$ be the image of the point $P(\mathbf{i}+3 \mathrm{k})$ in the plane $\mathbf{r} \cdot(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})=1$. Then, $P Q$ is normal to the plane. Since, $P Q$ passes through $P$ and in normal to the oiven plane, therefore equation of $P Q$ is $\mathbf{r}=(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{)}+\lambda(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})$
Since, $Q$ lies on the line $P Q$, so let the position vector of $Q$ be $(\mathbf{i}+3 \mathbf{k})+\lambda(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})$ i.e., $(1+\lambda) \mathbf{i}+\lambda \mathbf{j}+(3+\lambda) \mathbf{k}$. Since, $R$ is the mid-point of $P Q$, therefore position vector of $R$ is $\begin{aligned} & \frac{(1+\lambda) \mathbf{i}+\lambda \mathbf{j}+(3+\lambda) \mathbf{k}+\mathbf{i}+3 \mathbf{k}}{2} \\ & =\left(\frac{\lambda+2}{2}\right) \mathbf{i}+\frac{\lambda}{2} \mathbf{j}+\left(\frac{6+\lambda}{2}\right) \mathbf{k} \\ & =\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}+1\right) \mathbf{i}+\frac{\lambda}{2} \mathbf{j}+\left(3+\frac{\lambda}{2}\right) \mathbf{k}\end{aligned}$ Since, $R$ lies on the plane $\mathbf{r} \cdot(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})=1\therefore \quad\left[\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}+1\right) \mathbf{i}+\frac{\lambda}{2} \mathbf{j}+\left(3+\frac{\lambda}{2}\right) \mathbf{k}\right]\cdot(\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad\left[\frac{\lambda}{2}+1+\frac{\lambda}{2}+3+\frac{\lambda}{2}\right]=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \lambda=-2\end{aligned}$ Hence, the position vector of $Q$ is $-\mathbf{i}-2 \mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k}$.

Direction of current will be the direction of flow of $\mathrm{Ne}^{+}$ion i. e. towards right.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron is accelerated through a potential difference of 200 V . If $e / m$ for the electron be $1.6 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{kg}$, the velocity acquired by the electron will be
questions.solution:
$V=200 \mathrm{~V}, \frac{e}{m}=1.6 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{kg}$
Kinetic energy of electron $=\mathrm{eV}$ i.e, $\quad \frac{1}{2} m v^2=e V$
or $v^2=\frac{2 e}{m} V\quad \begin{aligned} \text{or} \quad v & =\sqrt{2 \frac{e}{m} V} \\ & =\sqrt{2 \times 1.6 \times 10^{11} \times 200} \\ & =8 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 10 m long copper wire while remaining in the east-west horizontal direction is falling down with a speed of $5.0 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field $=0.3 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$ the emf developed between the ends of the wires is
questions.solution:
Given, $l=10 \mathrm{~m}, v=5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

and $\quad H=0.3 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$ Induced emf $e=H v l\begin{aligned} & =0.3 \times 10^{-4} \times 5 \times 10 \\ & =1.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~V} \\ & =1.5 \mathrm{mV}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A coil having an area of $2 \mathrm{~m}^2$ is placed in a magnetic field which changes from $1 \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$ to $4 \mathrm{~Wb} / \mathrm{m}^2$ in 2 s . The emf induced in the coil will be
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Induced emf } e=n A \frac{d B}{d t} \\ & A=\text { area of coil }=2 m^2 \\ & \text { and } \\ & \qquad e=\frac{n=1}{2}+\frac{1 \times(4-1)}{2}=3 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solenoid has an inductance of 60 H and a resistance of $30 \Omega$. If it is connected to a 100 V battery, how long will it take for the current to reach $\frac{e-1}{e}=63.2 \%$ of its final value?
questions.solution:
Given, $\begin{aligned} & L=60 \mathrm{H} \\ & R=30 \Omega \\ & V=100 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$
In $L-R$ circuit current to reach $63.2 \%$ of its final value in time constant. Equation of current in $L-R$ circuit $I=I_0\left(1-e^{-R t / L}\right)$ Required time $=$ time constant $=\frac{L}{R}=\frac{60}{30}=2 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Millikan's oil drop experiment, an oil drop carrying a charge $Q$ is held stationary by a potential difference 2400 V between the plates. To keep a drop of half the radius stationary, the potential difference had to be made 600 V . What is the charge on the second drop?
questions.solution:
Force on charge, $F=Q E$
or $F=\frac{Q V}{d} \quad(\because V=E d)$
For drop to be stationary, 
weight of drop = force due to charge i.e., $\quad m g=\frac{Q V}{d}$
For two drops, $\frac{Q_1}{Q_2} \cdot \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\frac{m_1}{m_2}\frac{Q_1}{Q_2} \cdot \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\frac{\frac{4}{3} \pi r_1^3  \rho}{\frac{4}{3} \pi r_2^3 \rho}\frac{Q_2}{Q_1}=\frac{r_2^3}{r_1^3} \times \frac{V_1}{V_2}\therefore \quad \frac{Q_2}{Q}=\frac{(r / 2)^3}{r^3} \times \frac{2400}{600}Q_2=\frac{Q}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge of $10^{-9} \mathrm{C}$ is placed on each of the 64 identical drops of radius 2 cm . They are then combined to form a bigger drop. Its potential will be
questions.solution:
Volume of bigger drop = volume of 64 small drops i.e., $\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3=64 \times \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3$
or $\quad R=4 r$
Potential on small drop
$V_1=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q}{r}$
Potential on bigger drop
$\begin{aligned} V_2 & =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{64 q}{R} \\ V_2 & =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{64 q}{4 r} \\ & =\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 64 \times 10^{-9}}{4 \times 2 \times 10^{-2}} \\ & =7.2 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Millikan's oil drop experiment, a charged drop of mass $1.8 \times 10^{-13} \mathrm{~kg}$ is stationary between its plates. The distance between its plates is 0.9 cm and potential difference is 2000 V . The number of electrons in the drop is
questions.solution:
Drop is stationary, i.e., weight of drop = electric force
i.e., $\quad m g=q E$
or $\quad m g=q \frac{V}{d}$
or $\quad m g=n e \frac{V}{d}\therefore \quad n=\frac{m g d}{e V}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1.8 \times 10^{-13} \times 10 \times 0.9 \times 10^{-2}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 2000} \\ n & =50\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Escape velocity from earth's surface is $11 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{s}$. If radius of a planet is double than that of earth and density is same as that of earth, then the escape velocity from this planet will be
questions.solution:
Escape velocity $\begin{aligned} v_e & =\sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{R}} \\ & =R \sqrt{\frac{8}{3} G \rho}\end{aligned}\therefore \quad v \propto R$
We can say, if radius of a planet is double than that of earth then escape velocity from this planet will be $22 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: How much energy will necessary for making a body of 500 kg escape from the earth? $\left(g=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right.$, radius of the earth $=6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m}$ )
questions.solution:
Given $m=500 \mathrm{~kg}, g=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
AND $R_e=6.4 \times 10^6 \mathrm{~m}$
Energy required to scape
$\begin{aligned} E & =m g R_e \\ & =500 \times 9.8 \times 6.4 \times 10^6 \\ & =3.1 \times 10^{10} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 5 mol of hydrogen gas is heated from $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ at constant pressure. Heat given to the gas is (given $R=2 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{deg}$ )
questions.solution:
$Q=n C_p \Delta T$
For hydrogen
$C_p=\frac{7}{2} R$
So,
$\begin{aligned} Q & =n \frac{7}{2} R \Delta T \\ & =5 \times \frac{7}{2} \times 2 \times 30 \\ & =1050 \mathrm{cal}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle moves in the $x y$-plane under the action of a force $F$ such that the components of its linear momentum $\mathbf{p}$ at any time $t$ are $p_x=2 \cos t, p_y=\sin t$. The angle between $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{p}$ at time $t$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & p_x=2 \cos t, p_y=2 \sin t \\ & \begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \mathbf{p}=p_x \mathbf{i}+p_y \mathbf{j} \\ &=2 \cos t \mathbf{i}+2 \sin t \mathbf{j}\end{aligned} \\ & \text { Force }=\text { rate of change of momentum } \\ & \quad=\frac{d \mathbf{p}}{d t}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \mathbf{F}=-2 \sin t \mathbf{i}+2 \cos t \mathbf{j} \\ & \therefore \cos \theta=\frac{\mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{p}}{|\mathbf{F}| \cdot|\mathbf{p}|} \\ & =\frac{(-2 \sin t \mathbf{i}+2 \cos t \mathbf{j})(2 \cos t \mathbf{i}+2 \sin t \mathbf{j})}{\sqrt{4 \sin ^2 t+4 \cos ^2 t} \sqrt{4 \cos ^2 t+4 \sin ^2 t}} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \cos \theta=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \theta=90^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three blocks of masses $m_1, m_2$ are connected by massless strings as shown on a frictionless table. They are pulled with a force $T_3=40 \mathrm{~N}$. If $m_1=10 \mathrm{~kg}, m_2=6 \mathrm{~kg}$ and $m_3=4 \mathrm{~kg}$, the tension $T_2$ will be
questions.solution: Given : \(T_3=40 \mathrm{~N}, \mathrm{~m}_1=10 \mathrm{~kg}, \mathrm{~m}_2=6 \mathrm{~kg}\) and \(\mathrm{m}_3=4 \mathrm{~kg}\) Acceleration of complete system Total mass of system, \(\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2+\mathrm{m}_3=10+6+4=20 \mathrm{~kg}\) Acceleration of system =a Applying Newton's law, \(\Sigma \mathrm{F}=\mathrm{ma}\) \(\therefore \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_3}{\mathrm{~m}}=\frac{40 \mathrm{~N}}{20 \mathrm{Kg}}=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\) Calculation of \(\mathrm{T}_2\) From F.B.D OF \(\left(m_1+m_2\right)\) Force \(T_2\) is pulling 1 and 2 blocks. If we consider \(m_1\) and \(m_2\) as a system then \(T_1\) will get cancel as \(T_1\) acts as internal force. (As shown in figure) Therefore from Newton's second law- \(\begin{aligned} \Sigma \mathrm{F} & =\mathrm{ma} \\ \mathrm{~T}_2 & =\left(\mathrm{m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2\right) \mathrm{a}=(10+6) \times 2=32 \mathrm{~N} \end{aligned}\) Hence, Option (D) is correct answer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two parallel conductors $A$ and $B$ of equal length carry currents $i$ and $10 i$, respectively, in the same direction. Then
options: $A$ and $B$ will repel each other with same force
$A$ and $B$ will attract each other with same force
$A$ and $B$ will attract each other with different forces
questions.solution:
The magnitude of force acting on length $l$ of each conductor due to other is $\frac{F}{l}=\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi} \frac{i_1 i_2}{r}$

$\begin{array}{ll}\text { Given } & i_1=i, i_2=10 i \\ \therefore & \frac{F}{l}=\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi} \frac{10 i^2}{r}\end{array}$
From Fleming's left hand rule, this is force of attraction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton and an $\alpha$-particle enter a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with the same speed. If proton takes $25 \mu \mathrm{~s}$ to make 5 revolutions, then the periodic time for the $\alpha$-particle would be
questions.solution:
Time period of proton $T_p=\frac{25}{5}=5 \mu \mathrm{~s}$ 
By using $T=\frac{2 \pi m}{q B}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{T_\alpha}{T_p}=\frac{m_\alpha}{m_p} \times \frac{q_p}{q_\alpha}=\frac{4 m_p}{m_p} \times \frac{q_p}{2 q_p}=2 \\ & \Rightarrow  T_\alpha=2 T_p=10 \mu \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charged particle enters a magnetic field $H$ with its initial velocity making an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with $H$. The path of the particle will be
questions.solution: If charged particle enters in magnetic field making an angle less than $90^{\circ}$, then its path will be a helix.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A conducting wire is moving towards right in a magnetic field $B$. The direction of induced current in the wire is shown in the figure. The direction of magnetic field will be
options: in the plane of paper pointing towards right
in the plane of paper pointing towards left
perpendicular to the plane of paper and downwards
perpendicular to the plane of paper and upwards
questions.solution: According to Fleming's right hand rule, magnetic field will be perpendicular to the plane of paper and act downward.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electron moving with velocity $2 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, describes a circle in a magnetic field of strength $2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~T}$. If $\frac{e}{m}$ of electron is $1.76 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{kg}$. Then the diameter of the circle will be
questions.solution:
The force exerted on electron moving with velocity $v$ is
$F=e v B \sin \theta$
where $\theta=90^{\circ}\therefore \quad F_B=e v B$...(i)
Centripetal force is given by
$F_C=\frac{m v^2}{r}$...(ii)
Equating Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$r=\frac{m v^2}{e B}$
Diameter $d=2 r=\frac{2 v}{(e / m) B}\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad d^{\prime} & =\frac{2 \times 2 \times 10^7}{1.76 \times 10^{11} \times 2 \times 10^{-2}} \\ & =1.1 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Rn decays into Po by emitting an $\alpha$-particle with half-life of 4 days. A sample contains $6.4 \times 10^{10}$ atoms of Rn after 12 days, the number of atoms of Rn left in the sample will be

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: As a result of radioactive decay ${ }_{92} \mathrm{U}^{238}$ is converted into ${ }_{91} \mathrm{~Pa}^{234}$. The particles emitted during this decay are
questions.solution:
Decrease in mass number $=238-234=4$ No. of $\alpha$-particles emitted $=\frac{4}{4}=1$
Decrease in atomic number due to emission of $1 \alpha$-particle is 2 , but now atomic number is 91.
Hence, number of $\beta$-particles = $91+2$ - 92 = 1 .

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following pairs is an isobar?
questions.solution: Isobars are the elements which have same mass number. So, ${ }_{15} \mathrm{P}^{30}$ and ${ }_{14} \mathrm{Si}^{30}$ are isobars.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The half-life of the isotope ${ }_{11} \mathrm{Na}^{24}$ is 15 h .
How much time does it take for $\frac{7}{8}$ th of a sample of this isotope to decay?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Decáy constant of radium is $\lambda$. By a suitable process its compound radium bromide is obtained. The decay constant of radium bromide will be
questions.solution: Many nuclei are radioactive. This means that they are unstable like radium and will eventually decay by emitting as particle transforming the nucleus into another nucleus. A chain of decays take place until a stable nucleus is reached. In the compound radium bromide, radium is radioactive while bromide is not, hence decay constant of compound is same as that of radium that is $\lambda$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration of a particle performing SHM is $12 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}^2$ at a distance of 3 cm from the mean position. Its time period is
questions.solution: Acceleration $a=\omega^2 y\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad a & =\left(\frac{2 \pi}{T}\right)^2 y \\ \Rightarrow \quad T^2 & =\frac{4 \pi^2 y}{a} \\ \Rightarrow \quad T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{y}{a}} \\ & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{3}{12}} \\ T & =2 \pi \times \frac{1}{2}=3.14 \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}T=2 \pi \times \frac{1}{2}=3.14 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A thin prism $P_1$ of angle $4^{\circ}$ and refractive index $1.54^{\circ}$ is combined with another thin prism $P_2$ of refractive index 1.72 to produce dispersion without deviation. The angle of $P_2$ is
questions.solution:
Angle of deviation $\delta=(n-1) A$.
Dispersion produced by both the prism's will be equal.
$\begin{aligned}\left(n_1-1\right) A_1 & =\left(n_2-1\right) A_2 \\ \Rightarrow \quad A_2= & \frac{\left(n_1-1\right) A_1}{\left(n_2-1\right)}=\frac{(1.54-1)}{(1.72-1)}=3^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
Hence, the angle of prism $P_2$ is $3^{\circ}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: While viewing a distant object with a telescope suddenly a housefly sits on objective lens. The correct statement is that
options: housefly will be seen enlarged in image
housefly will be seen reduced in image
intensity of image will be decreased
intensity of image will be increased
questions.solution: If housefly sits on objective lens, then the intensity of image will decrease, because some of light rays will be stopped by housefly but housefly will not be seen.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A fish at a depth of 12 cm in water is viewed by an observer on the bank of a lake. To what height the image of the fish is raised?
(Refractive index of lake water $=\frac{4}{3}$ )
questions.solution: Apparent rise $=d\left(1-\frac{1}{a \mu_w}\right)\begin{aligned} & =12 \times\left(1-\frac{3}{4}\right) \\ & =12 \times \frac{1}{4}=3 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass $M$ is moving with a constant velocity on a line parallel to the $x$-axis. Its angular momentum with respect to the origin or $z$-axis
questions.solution:
Angular momentum of particle w.r.t. origin
$=$ linear momentum \times perpendicular distance of line of action of linear momentum from origin $=m v \times a=m v a=$ constant

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The orbital angular momentum of a satellite revolving at a distance $r$ from the centre is $L$. If the distance is increased to $16 r$, then the new angular momentum will be
questions.solution: $L=m v r=m \sqrt{\frac{G M}{r}} r=m \sqrt{G M r}\therefore \quad L \propto \sqrt{r}\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow  \frac{L_2}{L_1}  =\sqrt{\frac{r_2}{r_1}} \\  =\sqrt{\frac{16 r}{r}}=4 \\ \Rightarrow \quad  L_2  =4 L\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy gap between the valence and conduction bands of an insulator is about
questions.solution: An insulator has its valence band filled with electrons and its conduction band is empty. The energy gap is large approximately 5.0 eV , so it is not possible for ordinary process to provide enough energy for valence electrons to break out of their valence band and jump into the conduction band where they might carry electric current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For germanium crystal, the forbidden energy gap in joule is
questions.solution:
Forbidden energy gap for germanium crystal
$\begin{aligned} & =0.76 \mathrm{eV} \\ & =0.76 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J} \\ & =1.216 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The heat flows through a rod of length 50 cm and area of cross-section $5 \mathrm{~cm}^2$. Its ends are respectively at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The coefficient of thermal conductivity of the material rod is $0.092 \mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{m}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The temperature gradient of the rod is
questions.solution:
Temperature gradient of the rod
$\frac{\Delta \theta}{\Delta x}=\frac{\theta_2-\theta_1}{l}\therefore \quad \frac{\Delta \theta}{\Delta x}=\frac{125-25}{50}=\frac{100}{50}=2^{\circ} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The molar heat capacity of rock salt at low temperature varies with temperature according to Debye's $T^3$ law
Thus $C=k \frac{T^3}{\theta^3}$ where $k=1940 \mathrm{Jmol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1}\theta=281 \mathrm{~K}$
Calculate how much heat is required to raise the temperature of 2 moles of rock salt from 10 K to 50 K
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & d Q=n C d T \\ & \quad d Q=n k \frac{T^3}{\theta^3} d T \\ & Q=\frac{n k}{\theta^3} \int_{T_1}^{T_2} T^3 d T \\ & =\frac{n K}{\theta^3}\left(\frac{T_2^4-T_1^4}{4}\right)  \\ & =\frac{2 \times 1940 \times\left(50^4-10^4\right)}{(281)^3 \times 4} \\ & =272.79 \mathrm{~J}=273 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A soap bubble in vacuum has a radius of 3 cm and another soap bubble in vacuum has a radius of 4 cm . If the two bubbles coalesce under isothermal condition, then the radius of the new bubble is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two slits 4 mm apart, are illuminated by light of wavelength $6000 Å$. What will be the fringe width on a screen placed 2 m from the slits?
questions.solution:
Separation of slits $d=4 \mathrm{~mm}=4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$ Wavelength $\lambda=6000 Å=6 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~m}$
Distance of screen $D=2 \mathrm{~m}$ Fringe width $\beta=\frac{\lambda D}{d}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{6 \times 10^{-7} \times 2}{4 \times 10^{-3}} \\ & =3 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m} \\ & =0.3 \mathrm{~mm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An open pipe is suddenly closed at one end with the result that the frequency of third harmonic of the closed pipe is termed to be higher by 100 Hz than the fundamental frequency of the open pipe. The fundamental frequency of the open pipe is`
questions.solution:
Fundamental frequency of open pipe $n_1=\frac{v}{2 l}$
Frequency of third harmonic of closed pipe $\begin{aligned} n_1 & =\frac{3 v}{4 l} \\ \therefore \quad \frac{3 v}{4 l}-\frac{v}{2 l} & =100 \\ \frac{v}{4 l} & =100 \\ \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{v}{2 l}\right) & =100 \\ \therefore \quad n_1 & =200 \mathrm{~Hz}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fighter plane is moving in a vertical circle of radius $r$. Its minimum velocity at the highest point $A$ of the circle will be
questions.solution:
When a body tied to the end of a string is revolved in a vertical circle, the speed of the body is different at different points of the circular paths.

The resultant of tension $(T)$ and weight ( mg ) provides the necessary centripetal force i.e., $\quad T+m g=\frac{m v_A^2}{r}$
Tension ( $T$ ) becomes zero at the points of minimum velocity, therefore $\begin{aligned} & \therefore & 0+m g & =\frac{m v_A^2}{r} \\ & \Rightarrow & v_A & =\sqrt{g r}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In which case does the potential energy decrease?
options: On moving a body against gravitational force
On the rising of an air bubble in water
questions.solution: When an air bubble rises in water, it moves upward due to the buoyant force. As it rises, its gravitational potential energy might increase slightly, but the total potential energy (gravitational + potential energy from pressure) decreases because the bubble moves from a high-pressure region (deeper in water) to a lower-pressure region (near the surface).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Water is falling on the blades of a turbine at a rate of $100 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{s}$. If the height of the fall is 100 m , the power transferred to the turbine will be approximately
questions.solution:
Power $=\frac{\text { work }}{\text { time }}=\frac{m g h}{t}=\left(\frac{m}{t}\right) g h$
Given, $\frac{m}{t}=100 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{s}, h=100 \mathrm{~m}, g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\therefore$ Power $=100 \times 10 \times 100=100 \mathrm{~kW}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metre scale is standing vertically on the earth's surface on one of its end. It now falls on earth without slipping. Find the velocity with which the free end of the scale strikes the earth. $\left(g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Velocity of free end
$\begin{aligned} v & =\sqrt{3 g h} \\ & =\sqrt{3 \times 10 \times 1} \\ & =5.47 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A heavy mass is attached to a thin wire and is whirled in a vertical circle. The wire is most likely to break
options: when the mass is at the highest point of the circle
when the mass is at the lowest point of the circle
at an angle of $\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)$ from the upward vertical
questions.solution: The tension at the highest point is zero, but tension at the lowest point is 6 times the weight of the body. Hence, wire is most likely to break at the lowest point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The force constant of weightless spring is $16 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$. A body of mass 1.0 kg suspended from it is pulled down through 5 cm and then released. The maximum kinetic energy of the system (spring + body) will be
questions.solution:
Maximum KE of the system
= Maximum PE of the system
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{2} k x^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times\left(5 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & =2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
